tests/legacy_sass_entrypoint_ledger_prob.finding: These four controls do not establish their named ledger semantics: historicalFrames inequality is only a generic not-a-known-frame check and the physical owner rejects any candidate bytes before a stage predicate can be exercised. The maintained DATA helper legacy_sass_entrypoint_ledger_patch.py independently derives the one-row successor from the authentic before frame, checks summary counts and preservation of all unselected entry bytes, and exposes verify_sass_entrypoint_successor(candidate=...). A bounded regression can route these candidate faults through equivalent DATA verification and assert the corresponding predicate failure while retaining the real physical-owner rejection control separately.

No fault tail removal was identified in the five probes without ledger-candidate mutants. The four legacy Sass ledger-candidate controls still execute their rejection assertions, but currently prove only generic nonphysical rejection rather than named historical-stage semantics.
